heading: Self-repair can distort ablation-based estimates of component importance
definition: because of self-repair, ablation-based importance scores misstate what a component does.
summary: Three independent preprints support distortions in estimates of component importance using different methods, all on GPT-2 small's indirect object identification (IOI) task. None repeats the original comparison of direct contributions with total changes after ablation, and one reports only a small gain over masking subsets of components.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: untested. <1B: R2, from GPT-2-small IOI tests by studies with no author overlap with an original (arXiv:2607.01940, arXiv:2608.19338, arXiv:2610.04017); all use different (T2) methods on one task. 1-10B: R0, original only (arXiv:2307.15771, Chinchilla 7B, Counterfact). 10-100B and >100B: untested (counts: V7.studies_by_size has no such keys).
suggested_status.reason: The original (arXiv:2307.15771, Chinchilla 7B) reports low agreement between direct and ablation-based total effects (R7). Studies sharing no author with an original (counts: V7.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0) use different methods (counts: V7.tested_by_tranche T2 = 3) on a different family, GPT-2 small. They find that single-component ablation or NIE scores misrank backups: AUC 0.603±0.007 (arXiv:2607.01940#r6), and NIE Name Movers 0.14 vs Backups 0.74 (arXiv:2610.04017#r1-r2). They also find joint ablations non-additive, with I_PB 1.080 and I_PE 1.830 under mean ablation (arXiv:2608.19338#r1, r3). No challenges (counts: V7.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0). One limits_scope: arXiv:2608.19338#r12, where the gain over subset masks is small. All tests are preprints (counts: V7.tested_by_review_class preprint 4). The independent tests share one model and one task (IOI). No other group repeats the original's own direct-vs-total comparison.
suggested_status.open_questions: Several results would change the level. A different-group test on another family or size (Llama, Pythia, above 10B), or on general text rather than IOI, would extend it by scale. A same-method (T1) repeat of the original's direct-vs-total comparison would strengthen the 1-10B entry. A measure of how large the attribution error is across components and tasks is missing; all three independent studies list it as untested. More evidence that additive scores misstate little outside full-removal settings (as in arXiv:2608.19338#r12) would point to a narrower version. A study showing ablation scores match a reference despite backups would be a challenge.

source.title: The Hydra Effect: Emergent Self-repair in Language Model Computations
source.authors: Tom McGrath; Matthew Rahtz; János Kramár; Vladimir Mikulik; S. Legg

original_result.setup: The authors compared direct logit contributions read through the model's output mapping (unembedding) with total logit changes caused by resample ablation across all attention and MLP layers in Chinchilla 7B on Counterfact.
original_result.result: For the most likely token's logit, direct effects read through the output mapping (unembedding) and total effects measured by ablation disagreed substantially and correlated poorly. For most prompts and layers, the impact read through the unembedding exceeded the impact measured by ablation.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Ablating components individually understated the importance of components that compensate in GPT-2 small IOI.
Pinning (holding components fixed) reversed importance rankings between main and compensating components in GPT-2 small IOI.
In GPT-2 small IOI, ablating groups individually misstated their effects when other groups were also ablated.
Summing individual mean-ablation effects predicted joint effects well on one template, except with nearly everything removed.

wording_issues.issue: The statement is unqualified. On GPT-2 small IOI with template-conditioned mean ablation, adding P×B improves held-out subset-mask prediction from MAE 0.386 to 0.377 (r12), while P×E improves MAE by 0.1265 over the same masks (r13). The small average predictive contribution applies to P×B; it does not establish that substantial attribution errors occur only near full removal. Full group removals yield I_PB 1.080 logits (r1). Under mean ablation, Δ(E) is -2.270 logits (r8), and Δ(P+E) is -0.136 logits relative to clean (r9); E's conditional effect after P removal is Δ(P+E) − Δ(P).

No study in the pack isolates self-repair as the cause of the scoring error. arXiv:2608.19338's r2 note says the positive interaction is 'consistent with conditional backup and is als…' (truncated in the pack). Its r3 note ties I_PE to copy suppression. The original reports that early layers have large total but almost no direct effect (method-sensitivity and not-in-rows lines), a gap the pack does not attribute to compensation.

The studies measure the misstatement against different references: the unembedding-based direct effect (original, R7), documented backup labels (arXiv:2607.01940 r6), conditional and joint ablation effects (arXiv:2608.19338) and witness-integrated NIE (arXiv:2610.04017). 'Component' also varies: layers in the original, head groups in arXiv:2608.19338 and arXiv:2610.04017, single heads in arXiv:2607.01940 r6.

method_sensitivity.factor: Ablation replacement (template-conditioned mean, zero and resample)
method_sensitivity.what: In arXiv:2608.19338 the interaction terms are positive under both ablations, but their size differs: I_PB 1.080 (mean) vs 1.268 (zero) (r1, r2); I_PE 1.830 vs 1.681 (r3, r4). The joint P+E delta is -0.136 (mean) vs -0.769 (zero) (r9, r11). arXiv:2607.01940's method-sensitivity line says backup recovery varies with the ablation replacement operator. For GPT-2-small IOI, Appendix A.4.2, Table 7 reports resample single-ablation backup AUC 0.691±0.011 and resample CoAx AUC 0.961±0.008 (r12). These measure backup ranking, not restored-output fractions.

method_sensitivity.factor: Which interventions are scored (full group removal vs held-out subset masks) and which group-pair term is added
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2608.19338: full removals give I_PB of about 1 logit (r1, r7). Over held-out subset masks, adding P×B improves MAE by only 0.0083 (r12), while another pair term improves it by 0.1265 (r13). Its method-sensitivity line says the tested group-pair terms differ in predictive value.

method_sensitivity.factor: Scoring method: plain NIE vs witness-integrated (pinning)
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2610.04017: the primary-vs-backup ordering flips between plain NIE (Name Movers 0.14, Backups 0.74) and witness-integrated scores (1.16, 0.60) (r1, r2). Its method-sensitivity line says pinning all eligible witnesses lowers all three reported circuit scores on GPT-2 and Llama. On Qwen3 it improves net and reduces kill and faithfulness.

Original arXiv:2307.15771, Chinchilla 7B on Counterfact: Section 4.2 reports that direct and compensatory effects correlate well at intermediate layers. Early layers have large total but almost no direct effect; at very late layers, only the direct effect is non-negligible. Section 2.5 reports that unembedding-based and ablation-based importance lack correlation at all but late layers.

method_sensitivity.factor: Supplied primary set, output geometry and task/prompt setting
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2607.01940 (method-sensitivity line): backup recovery varies with the identity and contamination of the supplied primary set, the output geometry and the task/prompt setting. The pack gives no V7 rows for these variations.
